title: The Blues Scale
description: Add one gritty extra note to the minor pentatonic and you've got the sound of the blues.

steps.title: The blue note
steps.description: The blues scale is the minor pentatonic with one note squeezed in: the flat fifth, usually called the blue note. It sits right between the fourth and the fifth, and it's a big part of that bent, crying blues sound. In A, the notes are A, C, D, Eb, E, G.

steps.title: Play A blues
steps.description: Play up from A: A, C, D, Eb, E, G. When you hit Eb, listen to how it rubs, then relaxes as you step up to E.
steps.hint: Any octave works. Eb is the black key between D and E.

steps.title: Lean into the clash
steps.description: Play D and Eb together, in any octave. Two keys right next to each other clash on purpose. That crunch is a big part of how the blues sounds.
steps.hint: D is a white key, and Eb is the black key right above it.

steps.title: Play C blues
steps.description: Now move it to C: C, Eb, F, Gb, G, Bb. It's the same pattern of steps, so starting on C brings in more black keys.
steps.hint: The black keys here are Eb, Gb and Bb. The blue note is Gb, between F and G.

steps.title: Home base
steps.description: Play A minor (A, C, E). It's the home chord for the A blues scale, the place your blues phrases keep coming back to.
steps.hint: Thumb on A, middle finger on C, pinky on E.

steps.title: Find the blue note
steps.description: In the A blues scale, which note is the blue note?
